title: Stramash: A Fused-Kernel Operating System For Cache-Coherent, Heterogeneous-ISA Platforms
problem: Heterogeneous-ISA processors (e.g., x86+RISC-V or ARM+RISC-V on-chip) have required disjoint OS kernels per ISA with significant software coordination overhead, preventing advanced features like shared virtual memory and unified OS abstractions across ISA boundaries. Existing multi-kernel OS designs coordinate via message-passing rather than exploiting cache-coherent shared memory, leaving performance on the table.
motivation: Hardware heterogeneous-ISA systems are increasingly practical, but the software complexity of multi-kernel designs has limited both OS sophistication and hardware adoption; cache-coherent shared memory among heterogeneous-ISA CPUs provides an unexploited substrate for a unified OS design.
method: Stramash creates a single operating system kernel that runs on heterogeneous CPUs—ones using different instruction sets like x86 and RISC-V—by treating cache-coherent shared memory (memory that all CPUs can access and modify while staying synchronized) as its primary foundation. Unlike traditional multi-kernel operating systems that coordinate separate kernels through message-passing, Stramash puts its core data structures directly in shared memory and adds new mechanisms for synchronization, memory management, and task scheduling that work transparently regardless of which instruction set a CPU uses. The team built this by adapting Linux (Stramash-Linux) and validated it with a multi-ISA simulator (Stramash-QEMU) that achieves less than 4% average simulation error.
key_novelty: The fused-kernel OS unifies CPUs with different instruction sets by running a single operating system kernel built directly on cache-coherent shared memory, rather than coordinating separate kernels per ISA.
contributions: Fused-kernel OS design exploiting cache-coherent shared memory among heterogeneous-ISA CPUs as a unifying principle
New OS kernel mechanisms for ISA-transparent synchronization, scheduling, and memory management across ISA boundaries
Stramash-Linux prototype extending monolithic Linux to a fused-kernel across heterogeneous ISAs
Stramash-QEMU multi-ISA simulator with validated accuracy (<4% error); up to 2.1x speedup over multi-kernel OS on NPB benchmarks

metrics.speedup: up to 2.1x over multi-kernel OS on NPB benchmarks
metrics.accuracy: simulator validation: average <4% error vs. real hardware

baselines: state-of-the-art multi-kernel OS designs (e.g., McKernel, Popcorn Linux)
limitations: Evaluation is partially simulation-based (Stramash-QEMU) rather than fully on real heterogeneous-ISA hardware, and only NPB benchmarks are reported.
primary_theme: fused-kernel OS for cache-coherent heterogeneous-ISA platforms
